title: Humanoid Robots and China’s Vision of the Future
author: Leonie Spangenberg
text:
A robot competes in a track event at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, China, Aug. 22-26, 2026.
Credit: Baidu Baike
The robots lined up on the track. For a moment, it looked almost like an ordinary athletics meet. Then the race started. The machines lurched forward, their metal legs struggling to keep their balance as they sprinted toward the finish line. One of them, a Chinese humanoid robot called Tiangong Ultra, finished the 100 meters in 8.64 seconds – faster than Usain Bolt’s human world record.The scene took place this August at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, where more than 2,000 robots competed in 51 events. Some ran and boxed. Others performed household chores or industrial tasks. Some simply fell over. It was part sporting event, part technology demonstration, and part vision of the future. [...]
